questions.question: Giddha dance is mainly related to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Giddha** is a popular folk dance of **Punjab**, especially performed by women.
 
• Giddha is characterized by energetic movements and rhythmic clapping.
 
• It is usually performed during festivals and special occasions like weddings.
 
• The dance is accompanied by folk songs called 'Boliyan' that express various themes of life.
 
• Giddha is a representation of the rich cultural heritage of Punjab.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhangra**

 
 
• Bhangra is another popular folk dance from Punjab, typically performed by men.
 
• It is known for its high-energy movements and is usually performed during the harvest festival of Baisakhi.
 
 
 
• **Dandiya Raas**
 
 
• Originates from Gujarat.
 
• It is performed during the festival of Navratri with sticks called 'Dandiyas'.
 
 
 
• **Chhau**
 
 
• A traditional dance form from West Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand.
 
• Known for its masked dance performances.
 
 
 
• **Bihu**
 
 
• A folk dance from Assam.
 
• Performed during the Bihu festival, which marks the Assamese New Year.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of public sector industry in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL)** is one of India's largest public sector engineering and manufacturing enterprises.
 
• BHEL was established in 1964 and is owned and managed by the Government of India.
 
• It operates in the power, transmission, industry, transportation, renewable energy, oil & gas, and defense sectors.
 
• As a public sector undertaking, BHEL plays a significant role in the industrial development and energy sector of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)**

 
 
• PSUs are government-owned corporations or state-owned enterprises created to undertake commercial activities on behalf of the government.
 
• They are usually established through a special act of parliament or a government order.
 
• PSUs play a crucial role in the economic development of the country by providing essential services and infrastructure.
 
• Examples of major PSUs in India include BHEL, Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC).
 
 
 
• **Bajaj Auto**
 
 
• Bajaj Auto is a private sector automobile company in India.
 
• It is one of the largest manufacturers of two-wheelers and three-wheelers in the country.
 
• Bajaj Auto is part of the Bajaj Group and was founded in 1945.
 
 
 
• **Dabur**
 
 
• Dabur is a private sector company specializing in healthcare, personal care, and food products.
 
• It is one of the leading FMCG (Fast Moving Consumer Goods) companies in India.
 
• Dabur was founded in 1884 and is known for its Ayurvedic products.
 
 
 
• **Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO)**
 
 
• TISCO, now known as Tata Steel, is a private sector steel manufacturing company in India.
 
• It is part of the Tata Group and was established in 1907.
 
• Tata Steel is one of the largest steel producers in the world.

questions.question: Which among the following lakes is also known as the "Srinagar's Jewel"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Dal**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**Dal is a lake in Srinagar.

__
 
• It is an urban lake, which is the second largest in the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It is integral to tourism and recreation in Kashmir and is named the "Lake of Flowers", "Jewel in the crown of Kashmir" or "Srinagar's Jewel".

 [IMAGE: https://lp-cms-production.imgix.net/2019-06/384e10f39ebc6fab9b991467541ce8ed-dal-lake.jpg]

• Pangong Tso Lake, also popularly known as Pangong Lake is situated 160kms from Leh.

• Wular Lake is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia.
 
 
• It is sited in the Bandipora district in Jammu and Kashmir, India.
 
• The lake basin was formed as a result of tectonic activity and is fed by the Jhelum River.
 
 

**Vembanad:**

questions.question:
Match List I with List II:

 
 

 
 LIST I
 
 LIST II
 
 

 A.
 phonetics 
 I.
 Kalpa
 
 

 B.
 metre 
 II.
 nirukta
 
 

 C.
 etymology
 III.

 D.

questions.solution:
The correct matching is __**A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **phonetics:__**

 __
 
• ​Phonetics, also known as "**Shiksha**" in Sanskrit, is a fundamental branch of linguistics that deals with the **study of speech sounds**.
 
• It focuses on the physical properties of sounds, their production, perception, and the ways in which they are organized in different languages.
 
• Phonetics analyzes the articulatory, acoustic, and auditory aspects of speech, examining how sounds are made using the vocal tract, how they are transmitted through the air as sound waves, and how they are perceived by the human ear.
 
• By understanding the principles of phonetics, linguists and language learners can unravel the intricate details of pronunciation, phonological systems, and the rules governing sound patterns in languages worldwide.
 
 
 
• **metre:**__​
 __
 
• ​Metre, known as "**Chhanda**" in Sanskrit, refers to the rhythmic patterns and structures found in poetry.
 
• It is a crucial aspect of prosody, the study of poetic meters and verse forms.
 
• Metre determines the arrangement and organization of stressed and unstressed syllables in a line of poetry, creating a specific rhythm and musicality.
 
• In Indian classical literature, various chhandas or poetic meters have been defined, such as **Anushtubh, Doha, and Shloka**, each with its own set of rules and patterns.
 
• These metres provide a framework for poets to create harmonious and aesthetically pleasing verses.
 
• By employing different chhandas, poets can evoke specific moods, emphasize certain words or ideas, and create a captivating flow of language that enhances the overall beauty and impact of their poetic compositions.
 
 
 
• **​etymology:**__
 __
 
• **​Nirukta** is a Sanskrit term derived from the root words "ni," meaning "down," and "rukti," meaning **"to explain" or "to interpret."**
 
• It refers to the ancient Indian discipline of etymology, specifically focused on the interpretation of Vedic texts.
 
• Nirukta is attributed to **Yaska, a renowned sage** and grammarian from around the 6th century BCE.
 
• Yaska's work, also titled Nirukta, provides detailed explanations of the meanings and origins of words found in Vedic literature.
 
• It serves as a valuable source for understanding the linguistic, cultural, and religious aspects of ancient India.
 
• The term "nirukta" is now commonly used to denote the study of etymology in Sanskrit and other languages.
 
 
 
• **​ritual:**__
 
 
• ​**Kalpa** is a Sanskrit word derived from the root "klp," meaning "to arrange" or "to ordain."
 
• In Hinduism, it refers to the branch of ritualistic literature known as Kalpa Sutras, which provides detailed guidelines for performing various rituals, ceremonies, and sacraments.
 
• **Kalpa Sutras** are considered an integral part of the Vedas and are attributed to different sages and scholars.
 
• They cover a wide range of topics, including rites of passage, fire rituals, temple construction, marriage ceremonies, and more.
 
• 
 
Kalpa plays a vital role in preserving the traditions and practices of Hindu rituals, ensuring their proper execution and adherence to established customs and procedures.

 
 
 

Therefore the correct matching is 

 
 

 
 **LIST I**
 
 **LIST II**
 
 

 **A.**
 **phonetics **
 **I.**
 ** Shiksha**
 
 

 **B.**
 **metre **
 **II.**
 ** chhanda**
 
 

 **C.**
 **etymology**
 **III.**
 **nirukta**
 
 

 **D.**
 **ritual**
 **IV.**
 **Kalpa**

questions.question: Name the brightest star in the sky.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Sirius'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​**Sirius**, also known as **Alpha Canis Majoris **or **Dog Star**, is the **brightest star in the night sky **from Earth.
 
• Its apparent **visual magnitude is -1.46,** which is twice that of the second brightest star, the Canopus Star.
 
• It is actually a twin star in the **Canis Major constellation. **
 
• The **Sirius** is at a distance of about 8.6 light-years from Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Stars are made up of hot burning gases.
 
• They emit light of their own.
 
• A constellation is a group of stars forming a recognizable pattern.
 
• At present, 88 constellations are recognized.

 

 
 

 **Polaris**
 Also known as **North Star**. Unlike all the other stars in the sky, it is located at the same place i.e. above the North Pole every night from dusk to dawn, neither rising nor setting.
 
 

 **Antares**
 Also known as **Alpha Scorpii**. It is red and one of the largest known stars. It is the brightest star of the Zodiac constellation Scorpius.
 
 

 **Proxima Centauri**
 It is the nearest star to the Earth situated at 4.3 light-years away. It is in the southern constellation **Centaurus**.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• **Sun **is the brightest star.
 
• The brightest star in the night sky is **Sirius**.

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Constitution provides for Anti-Defection Law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__10th.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tenth Schedule** - popularly known as the Anti-Defection Act - was included in the Constitution via the** 52nd Amendment Act, of 1985**.
 
• It sets the provisions for disqualification of elected members on the grounds of defection to another political party.
 
• The anti-defection law punishes individual Members of Parliament (MPs)/MLAs for leaving one party for another.
 
• It allows a group of MP/MLAs to join (i.e., merge with) another political party without inviting the penalty for defection.
 
• As per the **1985 Act**, a 'defection' by one-third of the elected members of a political party was considered a 'merger'.
 
• **The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, of 2003**, changed this and now at least two-thirds of the members of a party must be in Favour of a "merger" for it to have validity in the eyes of the law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 **Description**
 
 

 1st
 The first schedule contains the list of states and union territories and their territories
 
 

 3rd
 The third Schedule contains the Forms of Oaths or Affirmations.
 
 

 7th
 This schedule deals with the three legislative lists: Union, State, and Concurrent.

questions.question: Which finance minister of Mughal emperor Akbar introduced the system of taxation called 'Dahsala'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Raja Todar Mal.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• ​__Raja Todar Mal was the finance minister of the Mughal emperor Akbar. 
 
• He introduced the Dahsala system of taxation in **1580 AD. **
 
• This system was based on the average production of different crops over the past 10 years. 
 
• The state's share was one-third of the average produce. 
 
• The Dahsala system was adopted in most of the provinces of the Mughal Empire, **except for the ones that were predominantly Muslim.**
 
• The Dahsala system was a **more efficient and equitable system of taxation** than the previous systems. 
 
• It helped to ensure that the state received a fair share of the revenue, while also protecting the interests of the farmers. 
 
• The Dahsala system was also one of the factors that **contributed to the economic prosperity** of the Mughal empire during Akbar's reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Raja Todar Mal divided all cultivable land into four categories:

 

 
• Polaj__: It was the best land cultivated every year.
 
• __Parauti__: It was the land of the second category which was left uncultivated for one year or two so that it could recover its fertility.
 
• __Chachar__: It was left uncultivated for three to four years in order to make it cultivable.
 
• __**Banjar:**__ Land that was not fit for agriculture and was mostly left uncultivated for a long time.

questions.question: The members of the Rajya Sabha are elected for a term

options.text: determined by the state legislative assembly of a state

__
 
• The members of the Rajya Sabha are elected for a term of 6 years.

questions.question: Diwali falls in which of the following months of the Hindu calendar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Kartika.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Kartika:-**

 
 
• **​**Kartika month is believed to be a time of heightened devotion and spiritual practices.
 
• Many Hindus undertake special rituals, prayers, and penances during this month to seek blessings, purify themselves, and deepen their connection with the divine.
 
• The dates of Kartika month vary each year according to the Hindu lunar calendar.
 
• The exact timing of Kartika depends on the position of the moon and its phases.
 
• This is why the Gregorian calendar months of October and November roughly correspond to Kartika.

questions.question: What was the name of King Ashoka’s daughter whom he appointed to carry out the duties of a Buddhist missionary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanghamitra**__.

__
 
• **Sanghamitra was King Ashoka’s daughter was appointed to carry out the duties of a Buddhist missionary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ashoka (273 BC-232 BC):**

 
 
• He was the greatest Mauryan ruler, Governor of Taxila and Ujjain.
 
• His rule extended to the whole of the sub-continent except the extreme south.
 
 
• It also included **Afghanistan, Baluchistan, Kashmir and the valleys of Nepal.**
 
 
 
• Ashoka had himself formally crowned in **269 BC.**
 
• Under Ashoka, the **Mauryan Empire reached its climax.**
 
• Ashoka fought the Kalinga War in **261 BC** in the 8th year of his coronation.
 
 
• Later, he was moved by the massacre in this war and, therefore, abandoned the policy of physical occupation in favour of the policy of cultural conquest.
 
• **Bherighosa was replaced by Dhammaghosa.**
 
 
 
• He embraced Buddhism under** Upagupta.**
 
• He sent his son ***Mahendra ***and daughter ***Sanghamitra*** to** Ceylon** (Sri Lanka as Buddhist missionaries with a sapling of original peepal tree).
 
• He inaugurated Dhamma Yatras from the 11th year of his reign by visiting Bodh Gaya and also appointed*** Dhamma Mahamatras*** (officer of righteousness to spread the message of Dhamma).

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Militant Nationalists?

I. Most prominent of them were Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai.

II. The political work encouraged self-reliance. 

III. They didn’t have faith in the mass action.
questions.solution:
**Militant Nationalism: **The militant nationalist brought about a departure in the National movement by adopting more radical methods of agitation than those followed by the earlier moderates. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Important points related to Militant Nationalism -**

 
• The prominent leaders of this phase of the national movement were Bal **Gangadhar Tilak, Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipan Chandra Pal, and the Lala Lajpat Rai.**
 
• The new leadership believed and preached that Indians' trust relies on their own efforts, their own political activity, and their own sacrifices.
 
• Their political work and outlook **encouraged self-reliance **and self-confidence. Moreover, they possessed a **deep faith in the strength of the Indian people and mass action.**
 
• They, therefore, pressed for political work among the masses.
 
• They also denied that British rule could be reformed from within. Swaraj or independence was to be the goal of the resurgent national movement. 

**Hence, Statements I and II are correct.**

questions.question: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, famous Indian scientist's, autobiography is known as _______.

questions.question: The depositional feature of the wind is called _________.
questions.solution:
Wind is one of the agents of erosion and deposition in the earth's surface processes. When wind deposits sediments, it creates different landforms that vary in size, shape, and composition. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The depositional feature of the wind that is called Loess.
 
• **Loess is a fine-grained, wind-blown sediment **that is composed of silt-sized particles.
 
• It is deposited by the wind in areas with **little or no vegetation cove**r, such as deserts and glacial outwash plains.
 
• Loess deposits can be several meters thick and can cover large areas of land.
 
• They are often found in regions where wind erosion is common, and the particles can be carried over long distances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mushroom rocks:** Mushroom rocks are a type of geological formation that is created by weathering and erosion processes. They are characterized by their distinctive shape, which resembles a mushroom. In this context, we will discuss mushroom rocks and their formation.
 
• **Moraine: **Moraines are a type of landform created by glacial deposition. They are formed by the accumulation of sediments and rocks that have been transported by glaciers. In this context, we will discuss moraines and their formation.
 
• **Stacks:** Stacks are a type of geological landform that are formed by erosion. They are tall, narrow columns of rock that are separated from the mainland by the sea. In this context, we will discuss stacks and their formation.

questions.question: The Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) is:

options.text: A constitutional body under Article 243W mandated to regulate urban air quality in metropolitan regions.
A statutory regulator under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, exercising nationwide jurisdiction over air pollution control.
A temporary committee constituted by the Supreme Court to monitor compliance with directions on stubble burning and vehicular emissions.
A statutory body established by a specific Act of Parliament with jurisdiction over the NCR and adjoining areas to coordinate air quality management across States.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court sought the Union government’s response on proposals to shift coal-based industries out of Delhi-NCR and took note of long-term recommendations made by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) regarding thermal power plants and vehicular emissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• CAQM is a statutory body created by a dedicated Act of Parliament to coordinate, plan, implement and monitor measures for air quality management in the NCR and adjoining areas, cutting across State jurisdictions. **Hence, Option D is correct. **
 
• CAQM is not a constitutional body under Article 243W; urban local bodies have functions relating to public health and sanitation, but CAQM’s mandate flows from statute. **Hence, Option A is incorrect. **
 
• CAQM does not derive its powers from the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, nor does it exercise nationwide jurisdiction; its territorial remit is NCR and adjoining areas.** Hence, Option B is incorrect. **
 
• CAQM is not a court-appointed temporary committee; it is a permanent statutory authority. **Hence, Option C is incorrect. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• CAQM replaced the earlier EPCA mechanism for NCR with enforceable statutory powers.
 
• NCR includes Delhi and parts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.
 
• CAQM can issue binding directions to State governments and agencies for air quality measures.
 
• Long-term measures discussed include curbs on coal-based thermal plants near NCR, vehicular emission control and stubble-burning mitigation.

questions.question:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : Rajatarangini's description of the 12th Century history of Kashmir mention five women rulers.

Reason (R) : Didda's career is described in the sixth taranga of Rajatarangini.

In the context of the above statements, which of the following is true ?

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct, but (R) is not correct
(R) is correct, but (A) is not correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **b**__**o**th (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Rajatarangini is a historical chronicle** of the kings of Kashmir **written by Kalhana in the 12th century. **
 
• **Statement (A) is accurate **as Rajatarangini indeed mentions five women rulers in its description of the 12th Century history of Kashmir. These women rulers were **Sugandha, Didda, Kota, Chaka, and Kallar.**
 
• **Statement (R) is also correct** **as Didda's career is indeed described in the sixth taranga **or canto of Rajatarangini.
 
• Didda was a prominent queen of Kashmir who ruled for an extended period, and her career is described in detail in the chronicle.
 
• 
 
**Moreover, Statement (R) provides a direct explanation for Statement (A)** by stating that Didda's career is mentioned in Rajatarangini, which is part of the chronicle that describes the five women rulers, making (R) the correct explanation of (A).

 

**Therefore, Option 1, "Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)," is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The Vajra Corps, which celebrated its 76th Raising Day on March 1, 2026, was raised in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1950.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Event:** The **Vajra Corps** celebrated its **76th Raising Day** on March 1, 2026.
 
• **Significance:** It was raised on **March 1, 1950**, at Ambala, and later moved to its permanent headquarters in **Jalandhar**, Punjab.
 
• **Historical Milestone:** It holds the distinction of being the **first Corps raised in the Indian Army after Independence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Operational Highlights__**

__
 
• **Nickname:** Popularly known as the **"Defenders of Punjab"**, the Corps is responsible for the security of the strategic Western Front.
 
• **Wars:** The Corps has participated in all major post-independence conflicts, most notably the **1965 and 1971 Indo-Pak Wars**, earning numerous Battle and Theatre Honours.
 
• **Motto:** The Corps is renowned for its spirit of sacrifice and valor, maintaining its position as a elite formation of the Western Command.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Context__**

 
• **Western Command:** Vajra Corps is one of the key pillars of the Indian Army's Western Command.
 
• **Battle Honours:** It has been awarded 25 Battle Honours and 38 Theatre Honours for its exceptional performance in various operations.
